title: eras.json demand_era binding is never read at runtime — the demand director keys demand.eras[state.era-1] directly, so the declared cross-ref can silently diverge
evidence: core/demand.odin:52: `de := &cat.demand.eras[era-1]` (scripted_plan_demand; same direct keying at core/health.odin:117, core/warnings.odin:239, core/crisis.odin:337). A repo-wide grep for `demand_era` outside tests hits only the load path in core/catalog.odin (lines 346, 365, 1079, 1146-1153) — no runtime reader exists. The load validates only existence: `if de < 1 || de > i32(len(cat.demand.eras))` (catalog.odin:1151), never demand_era == era. The diff's own test table encodes the divergence: core/era_test.odin:51 `make_row(cat, 4, "real_time", "Real-Time", 3, ...)` — era 4 binds demand era 3, yet at state.era=4 scripted_plan_demand returns an empty plan (`if era == 0 || int(era) > len(cat.demand.eras)` demand.odin:49), not the bound row.
detail: The era table declares a demand-signature binding the sim ignores: runtime truth is 'demand row index == state.era'. An eras.json row binding era N to demand_era M (N != M) passes load but the sim spawns demand row N — the two-source drift the story's invariants were built to prevent.
recommended_fix: Pick one source of truth: either key the director through cat.eras[era-1].demand_era, or enforce demand_era == era at load (fail-fast), or drop the field and document index equality as the contract.

title: Era-table gaps pad to empty Era_Row{} that era_advance_validate and era_row accept as valid advance targets
evidence: core/catalog.odin:1243: `for len(cat.eras) < int(era) { append(&cat.eras, Era_Row{}) }` — gaps pad with zero rows and no contiguity check exists (only the duplicate `seen[era-1]` guard at 1113/1116). core/era.odin:52: `if c.to_era == 0 || int(c.to_era) > len(cat.eras) {` — 'in the table' means '<= the padded length', so a sparse eras.json (rows 1 and 3) makes to_era=2 pass validation; era_step then fires into a ghost era whose era_row lookup returns ok=true (core/catalog.odin:1350-1355 returns `&cat.eras[era-1], true` for the padded row, era==0, empty rosters).
detail: Validation couples to the padded array length rather than row existence, so an advance into a gap era latches and fires with an empty unlock/roster row (and the demand director then reads a possibly-empty demand row). Latent — current data is contiguous — but the new FSM surface bakes the hole in.
recommended_fix: Reject non-contiguous era tables at load (each stored row's era must equal its index+1, no padded gaps), or make era_advance_validate/era_row treat a padded row (row.era == 0) as absent.
